newsitem.title: USA: Bristol-Myers to form new worldwide units.
newsitem.headline: Bristol-Myers to form new worldwide units.

text.p: Bristol-Myers Squibb Co said on Tuesday that it formed new business divisions, effective January 1, 1997, as part of a transition from the upcoming retirement of executive vice president Michael Autera.

Autera, who is retiring in June 1997, has been responsible for Mead Johnson Nutritionals, Zimmer and ConvaTec since January 1994, and for Worldwide Consumer Medicines, Clairol and Matrix Essentials since September 1994, Bristol-Myers said.

Kenneth Weg, executive vice president, will become president of the newly formed Worldwide Medicines Group, which will include the Worldwide Pharmaceutical Group, Worldwide Consumer Medicines and the central and eastern European units, the drug company said.

Peter Dolan will become president of the newly formed Nutritional and Medical Devices Group, assuming the additional responsibility for the Zimmer and ConvaTec medical devices businesses, Bristol-Myers said.
Bristol-Myers Squibb's Worldwide Beauty Care Group was formed on September 12, 1996. That unit, which makes Clairol and Matrix Essentials, is headed by Stephen Sadove, the company said.
